$comment: Curated input to `navgator arch-index`. This is the ONE hand-maintained file in the
architecture index: humans write intent (what a module is for, which boundaries must
hold), the generator supplies every number and every edge. Regeneration is still
deterministic because this file is an INPUT, not an output.
modules[]    id + path + one-sentence responsibility. A file is assigned to the LONGEST
matching path prefix, so a curated parent claims its whole subtree until a
child is curated too — splitting a module is an edit here, not a code change.
A path no curated prefix covers falls back to its first two path segments and
shows up as 'uncurated' in ARCHITECTURE.md, which is how a new top-level
boundaries[] Rules the generator re-checks on every run. A violation is printed with the
exact importing file, and CI fails on any drift in the generated output.

modules.responsibility: Repo-root configuration only (tsconfig, vitest config, package manifests). `.` claims top-level files and nothing below them.
Core library and the published npm surface: scan orchestration, storage, graph queries (impact/trace/rules/review), and the shared type system.
The `navgator` binary. One module per subcommand, all registered in `src/cli/index.ts`; owns the five-value exit-code contract in `exit-codes.ts`.
Language and infrastructure scanners that turn source files into components and connections (TS/JS imports, Swift, Rust, Prisma, queues, cron, env, LLM calls).
Dependency-free statistical sampling and process-control math used to audit scan accuracy.
Tiered semantic mapping: emits LLM work packets for the calling agent to run, then validates and attributes the findings. Findings never enter the graph.
External-boundary enrichment: resolves npm/pip/cargo identities and versions against registries, cached machine-wide in `~/.navgator/`.
Concurrency-safe dirty ledger and drainer that decide whether stored architecture data is stale enough to rescan.
Canonical-main plus branch-delta snapshots, so an agent can separate committed architecture from uncommitted local change (`arch-diff`).
Opt-in MCP server. Deprecated as a default surface — the CLI is the agent interface; this ships only for consumers that cannot spawn a subprocess.
gator-memory: the durable cross-session narrative in `~/.navgator/memory/` (which projects exist, when, and what materially changed).
PageRank and Louvain community detection over the component graph; writes `metrics.json` and back-writes scores onto components.
SCIP overlay: shells out to scip-typescript for compiler-accurate cross-file edges the regex scanner cannot resolve.
Cross-repo sweep: runs the single-repo scan pipeline over a folder of repositories and joins the results into one dependency map.
Shallow-clones a GitHub URL into a cache and scans it. This is the untrusted-input path — every scanner cap in `src/scanners/scan-limits.ts` exists because of it.
Markdown projection of stored components. Pure derivative — the JSON store stays canonical.
Nested git repository inside `.navgator/` that gives architecture snapshots a history without touching the parent repo's git.
Vitest suite for the core library, CLI, and scanners. Imports production modules freely; nothing in production may import it.
Next.js dashboard (`navgator ui`), built and packaged separately from the CLI. Talks to stored architecture data through its own API routes, never by importing `src/`.
Dashboard routes and the loopback read-only HTTP API under `web/app/api/`.
Dashboard React components, including the vendored shadcn/ui primitives in `web/components/ui/`.
Dashboard React hooks shared across components.
Dashboard client and server helpers: API client, types, project-path resolution, and request guards.
Release and install tooling run from npm scripts and CI — the release verifier, web-runtime packaging, benchmarks, and host-plugin installers.

boundaries.why: `src` is the published library (`main`/`exports` in package.json). If it imported the CLI, every library consumer would pull in commander and the whole command surface.
Test helpers are not shipped in the `files` list, so a production import of one breaks the published package while passing locally.
The CLI and the dashboard are separate build units with separate tsconfigs. `src` importing `web` would put React and Next.js in the CLI's dependency path.
Scanners must stay callable as plain functions from the library, the MCP server, and tests. A dependency on the CLI layer would couple them to process state and exit codes.
The dashboard reads architecture data over its own loopback API, not by importing the scanner. Importing `src` would make the Next.js build depend on the CLI's compile output.
Same separation as `dashboard-not-core`, enforced at the route layer where the temptation to import the scanner directly is highest.
